Final extension of the mandate of the UN Mission to Support the Hodeidah Agreement (UNMHA) until 31 Mar. 2026

United Nations S/RES/2813 (2026) Security Council Distr.: General 27 January 2026

Resolution 2813 (2026) Adopted by the Security Council at its 10097th meeting, on 27 January 2026

The Security Council, Recalling and reaffirming all its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President concerning Yemen, including resolution 2786 (2025), Reaffirming its strong commitment to the unity, sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Yemen and its commitment to stand by the people of Yemen, Reaffirming its endorsement of the agreement reached in Sweden by the Government of Yemen and the Houthis on the City of Hodeidah and the Ports of Hodeidah, Salif, and Ras Issa (the Hodeidah Agreement), and reiterating its call on the parties to work cooperatively to implement all its provisions, Noting, in line with the Secretary-General’s letter of 10 June 2025 (S/2025/371) that the evolving context within Hodeidah and across Yemen, as well as the wider region and internationally, could create opportunities for further efficiencies and structural coherence and coordination across United Nations missions in Yemen, Recalling its intention to review the full range of options for UNMHA’s mandate, including assessing the future viability and sunsetting of the Mission, and make any necessary adjustments to gain efficiencies and reduce costs or otherwise as may be required to UN operations in Hodeidah by developments on the ground, including inter alia a durable nationwide ceasefire,

1. Takes note of the Secretary-General’s letter (S/2025/766) dated 25 November 2025 and decides to extend UNMHA’s mandate for a final two-month period until 31 March 2026, during which time the Mission will conduct the effective, efficient and safe drawdown of the Mission including ceasing of its operations, and required planning and preparation for transition of any residual functions to the Office of the Special Envoy, and the withdrawal of UNMHA personnel and assets and elimination of the permanent presence in Hodeidah, as mentioned in Option 3 of S/2025/766, and further decides, as of 1 April 2026, UNMHA will commence a liquidation process;

2. Requests the Secretary-General prepare, in consultation with the Yemeni parties, a transition and liquidation plan for UNMHA to start the transfer of its residual functions to The Office of the Special Envoy of the Secretary -General for Yemen (OSESGY), as well as the orderly and safe drawdown and withdrawal of its

26-01034 (E) *2601034*

S/RES/2813 (2026)

personnel and assets, including identification of an end date for liquidation of activities in Hodeidah;

3. Decides to authorize for a period to be determined based on administrative procedures subject to the UN Financial Rules and Regulations, and adequate to ensure an orderly and safe transition, the retention of necessary assets and capabilities to ensure continued structural coherence and coordination across remaining United Nations Missions in Yemen, and bearing in mind challenges that have directly impeded UNMHA’s capacity to deliver its mandate;

4. Recognizes that the safety of UN personnel remains of the utmost importance and calls on the Houthis to enable a safe and secure operating environment including through the immediate and unconditional release of all those detained;

5. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.
